title: Maru, looking back
hookLine: the raga of courage holds some of the Granth's longest hymns
tomorrow: what if every month of the year were a love letter?

cards: Courage shows up in the hands first. Sweaty palms before a talk. A tight grip on the wheel on a first drive.
A hand that won't let go of someone else's. Simran saw it this week in the smallest way. Fateh, her little cousin, tied his own patka for the first time, alone in front of the mirror.
It came out crooked. When she reached to fix it, he pulled away: no, mine. That's what courage feels like in your hands.
Maru, looked at one more time, is full of hands.

teach.b: Maru runs from ang 989 to ang 1106, and tradition links it with courage and the field of battle. It holds long hymns, the Solhe, and ballads, and the Bhagats at the end. Hold it up and look at the hands.
First, a coin in the palm: Guru Nanak's test, where real silver rings true whatever's scrawled on the paper.
Then cupped hands, the Anjulian, and the riddle of plenty and little. Hands over the eyes in the dark before creation, which turned out to be full.
A face turned toward the Guru, and a humble traveler's open hands, answering mockery with peace.
Bebe's floury hand, pressing one couplet into Simran's: when You are on my side. Kabir's warrior, who doesn't leave the field. And Ravidas, lifted under a canopy he didn't build.
Put together, Maru's courage is almost never a fist.

teach.h: A HAND THAT DOESN'T LET GO.
teach.b: It's a hand that trusts, receives, holds on, and refuses to let go of what's right.

how: Hymns in raga Maru are sung in kirtan at the gurdwara and read in order during a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib; Kabir's true-warrior salok and Ravidas's 'who but You' are often heard among them.

o: an evening raga of short hymns and longing
the raga tradition ties to courage, ang 989 to 1106
a raga sung only at weddings and festivals

games.q: Maru in the hands — tap the pairs.
p: when You are on my side

s: Maru's courage is all about fighting battles
the pictures on this walk were of trust: a coin, cupped hands, a humble walk, a whispered couplet.
Maru ends with the Bhagats, Ravidas's 'who but You' among them
it holds the long Solhe and two ballads.

games.q: your friend is learning to drive and stalls the car in front of everyone. she says she's not brave enough for this. what would Maru say about courage?
o: it's a steady hand that keeps holding on, stalls and all.
real courage is never stalling in the first place.
courage means hiding how scared you are from everyone.
games.why: Maru's courage is rarely a fist: a hand that trusts, receives, holds on, and doesn't leave the field.

practice: Choose your favorite Maru line from these days and say it once, slowly, while pressing your palms firmly together. Then let your hands fall open in your lap, palms up. Stay there, open but steady, for the rest of the sit.

carryVoice: For the road: brave in faith, an open hand that still holds on. Fifteen-seventy-nine, palms open.
